chunks: And with this chain of transmission:
That Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to judge concerning a zindīq

If two approved men testify against him, while a thousand testify to his innocence, the testimony of the two men is accepted and the testimony of the thousand is nullified, because it is a concealed religion.

key_terms.بِالْبَرَاءَةِ: attesting to innocence or freedom from the charge
key_terms.دِينٌ مَكْتُومٌ: a concealed creed or hidden religion
key_terms.زِنْدِيقٍ: a heretic or dissimulating unbeliever whose false creed is concealed

ai.seo_question: Why is the testimony of two reliable witnesses accepted against a zindīq even if many testify to his innocence?
ai.summary: This report states a legal ruling attributed to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding the case of a zindīq whose disbelief is hidden. It establishes that the testimony of two reliable witnesses is accepted over the exonerating testimony of many others, because the matter concerns a concealed creed not apparent to the public.
